title: Animation
description: Animation cinematography constructs light and motion instead of capturing them: graphic volume, designed keys, and movement as drawing, paint, or stepped CG, not as a photographed exposure. The world is built. Lens physics appear only if you choose them.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A drawing can hold a smear. A painted film can ignore a 180-degree shutter.
Spider-Verse can step the action and print halftone. Kaguya can let charcoal dissolve.
The 'camera' is a viewpoint in a constructed space. It is not Pixel Art (discrete sampling and a locked palette) and not Stop Motion (physical puppets moved a frame at a time).
Those are specific construction methods. Animation as a look means designed light and graphic motion, in 2D, 3D, or hybrid.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Decide the construction: 2D volumes, CG with graphic shaders, or mixed. Light is keyed in the design, not motivated only by a set practical unless you invent one.
Motion: smears, holds, stepped frame rates, or full 24fps. Do not default to photoreal ray-traced blur unless that is the film.
Prompt graphic volume, designed light, motion as drawing rather than photography.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the world must be constructed, not captured. Do not use it as a filter on live action that still wants real lens physics, and do not collapse it into pixel tiles or puppet stop-motion unless that is the method.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Animation is constructed motion and light. Pixel Art is tiled, paletted sampling.
Stop Motion is physical increment. Video Game is playable camera logic (follow cam, HUD, collision), which may be animated or live-action dressed as a game.
A photoreal CG shot that imitates a 50mm still is animation as production, not this graphic look.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is photoreal live action, Pixel Art, or Stop Motion. The tell is a 50mm bokeh plate, chunky sprites, or puppet seams you did not want.
Fix: specify the graphic medium, design the key as paint or shader, and choose smear or stepped motion.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Animation in film?
A constructed look: light and motion are designed (drawn, painted, or shaded), not captured through a lens, unless you deliberately simulate a lens. Graphic volume replaces photographic exposure.
Animation vs Pixel Art
Pixel art locks sampling and palette into visible tiles. Animation may be fluid charcoal, cel, or graphic 3D. Both are constructed. Only pixel art makes the pixel the unit of the world.
When should I use Animation?
When the world cannot or should not be a photographed place. Skip it if you want a real lens, if you want visible tiles, or if you want puppet stop-motion specifically.
How do I prompt Animation for AI image or video?
Write: Animated treatment of [Subject], graphic volume, designed light, motion as drawing rather than photography. Name charcoal, cel, or halftone. Do not request photoreal bokeh by default.
